paragraphs.title: Opening of the Psalm and the Cry to God

answers: O LORD God of his salvation
easy.explanation: The psalm begins, “O LORD God of my salvation, I have cried day and night before thee.”
easy.q: To whom does the psalmist cry?

easy.explanation: He says that he has cried before the LORD “day and night.”
easy.q: When does the psalmist cry before the LORD?

easy.explanation: He prays, “incline thine ear unto my cry.”
easy.q: What does the psalmist ask the LORD to incline?

medium.explanation: He asks, “Let my prayer come before thee.”
medium.q: What does the psalmist want to come before the LORD?

medium.explanation: Verse 3 says, “For my soul is full of troubles.”
medium.q: What is the condition of the psalmist’s soul?

answers: His life is drawing near to the grave
His prayer is drawing near to the temple
His friends are drawing near to him
medium.explanation: He says, “my life draweth nigh unto the grave.”
medium.q: What does the psalmist say is drawing near?

answers: The psalmist is deeply troubled, yet he continues to pray to God
The psalmist is joyful and avoids prayer
The psalmist trusts only in his acquaintances
challenge.explanation: Although his soul is full of troubles and death seems near, he continues crying to the LORD.
challenge.q: What contrast is presented in these verses?

answers: His prayer is limited to one time
He is speaking about a journey
challenge.explanation: “Day and night” emphasizes that his cry to God continues without interruption.
challenge.q: What does the repeated reference to day and night suggest?

answers: A troubled person urgently asks God to hear him
challenge.explanation: The opening combines urgent prayer, deep trouble, and a plea for God’s attention.
challenge.q: Which description best summarizes the opening of the psalm?

paragraphs.title: Life on the Edge of Death and the Pit of Darkness

answers: Them that go down into the pit
Those who sing in the temple
easy.explanation: He says, “I am counted with them that go down into the pit.”
easy.q: With whom does the psalmist say he is counted?

easy.explanation: He describes himself as a man “that hath no strength.”
easy.q: What does the psalmist say he has no?

easy.explanation: Verse 6 says, “Thou hast laid me in the lowest pit.”
easy.q: Where does the LORD lay the psalmist?

answers: As the slain that lie in the grave
medium.explanation: The verse compares them with “the slain that lie in the grave.”
medium.q: How are the dead described in verse 5?

answers: The lowest pit, darkness, and the deeps
A palace, a garden, and a river
A city, a field, and a mountain
medium.explanation: Verse 6 names “the lowest pit,” “darkness,” and “the deeps.”
medium.q: What three images describe the place where the psalmist has been laid?

medium.explanation: The psalmist says, “thou hast afflicted me with all thy waves.”
medium.q: What has the LORD afflicted the psalmist with?

answers: It moves from weakness and nearness to death into the lowest darkness
It moves from sorrow into celebration
It moves from isolation into friendship
challenge.explanation: The psalmist first describes having no strength and being counted among the dead, then being placed in darkness and the deep.
challenge.q: How does the description develop from verses 4 through 6?

answers: It portrays trouble as overwhelming and surrounding him
It shows that the psalmist has found safety
challenge.explanation: The waves represent affliction that crashes over and overwhelms the psalmist.
challenge.q: What does the imagery of the waves add to the description of suffering?

challenge.explanation: These expressions create an image of extreme depth, darkness, and helplessness.
challenge.q: Which overall feeling is created by “the lowest pit,” “darkness,” and “the deeps”?

paragraphs.title: Isolation, Distress, and Questions about the Dead

answers: They have been put far from him
They have joined him in the pit
easy.explanation: The psalmist says, “Thou hast put away mine acquaintance far from me.”
easy.q: What has happened to the psalmist’s acquaintances?

easy.explanation: He says, “LORD, I have called daily upon thee.”
easy.q: What does the psalmist do daily?

easy.explanation: He says, “I have stretched out my hands unto thee.”
easy.q: What does the psalmist stretch out to the LORD?

medium.explanation: He asks, “shall the dead arise and praise thee?”
medium.q: What does the psalmist ask whether the dead can do?

answers: Whether God’s lovingkindness can be declared there
Whether the grave can become a palace
Whether his friends can live there
medium.explanation: He asks, “Shall thy lovingkindness be declared in the grave?”
medium.q: What does the psalmist question about the grave?

answers: A place or condition of ruin and death
medium.explanation: In the question about God’s faithfulness, “destruction” parallels the grave and the realm of death.
medium.q: What does the word “destruction” refer to in this passage?

answers: The psalmist is isolated from people but continues calling upon God
The psalmist is surrounded by friends but refuses to pray
The dead are praying while the living remain silent
challenge.explanation: Although his acquaintances are far from him, he continues to call upon the LORD.
challenge.q: What central contrast appears in verses 9 through 14?

answers: To express the urgency of his appeal while he is still alive
To describe a celebration among the dead
To explain how to prepare a burial
challenge.explanation: The questions emphasize his fear of death and the urgency of asking God for help.
challenge.q: Why does the psalmist ask several questions about the dead and the grave?

answers: He continues seeking God after the night has passed
He no longer wants God to hear him
challenge.explanation: He says, “in the morning shall my prayer prevent thee,” showing that his prayer continues.
challenge.q: What does the psalmist’s prayer in the morning show?

paragraphs.title: Enduring Suffering and the Loss of Every Connection

answers: Why He casts off his soul and hides His face
Why He gives him many friends
Why He leads him into celebration
easy.explanation: He asks, “LORD, why castest thou off my soul? why hidest thou thy face from me?”
easy.q: What does the psalmist ask the LORD in verse 15?

easy.explanation: He says, “I am afflicted and ready to die from my youth up.”
easy.q: From when has the psalmist been afflicted?

easy.explanation: The final verse says, “Lover and friend hast thou put far from me.”
easy.q: Who has been put far from the psalmist at the end of the psalm?

answers: They distract and cut him off
medium.explanation: The psalmist says, “I suffer thy terrors I am distracted,” and that the terrors have cut him off.
medium.q: What effect do the LORD’s terrors have on the psalmist?

answers: They rise like a mountain of gold
medium.explanation: He says, “They came round about me daily like water.”
medium.q: How are the psalmist’s troubles pictured in verse 17?

answers: His acquaintances are distant and unavailable to him
His acquaintances are lighting his way
His acquaintances are gathered in his house
medium.explanation: The phrase expresses the final loss of human companionship and the darkness surrounding the psalmist.
medium.q: What does “mine acquaintance into darkness” communicate?

answers: God’s hidden face and the loss of human relationships together portray abandonment
The question in verse 15 removes the theme of loneliness
Both verses describe a musical performance
challenge.explanation: The psalmist feels abandoned by God and also separated from every close human relationship.
challenge.q: How does verse 15 connect with the final verse?

answers: The trouble surrounds him continually and from every side
He has found a place of rest
He is about to escape from danger
challenge.explanation: The surrounding water represents persistent suffering that leaves him no place of relief.
challenge.q: What does the comparison to water emphasize?

answers: The psalmist moves from questioning God’s rejection to describing the loss of all human connections
He moves from loneliness to a new community
He moves from darkness to a clear solution
challenge.explanation: The section begins with questions about God’s hidden face and ends with lover, friend, and acquaintance far away in darkness.
challenge.q: What development occurs from the beginning to the end of this section?
